new_statements.rule_in_words: Non-contrastive stress on the last syllable of the root, regardless of syllable weight or openness; person/possessor prefixes and the clause-position/aspect suffixes lie outside the stress domain, so an unaffixed word is stressed on its final syllable while a suffixed word surfaces with penultimate (root-final) stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Only for noun collocations (N+N): primary (word) stress on the first lexeme, secondary stress on the second, e.g. /g-on kul/ ['gon,kul] 'his skull', p.107 ex. (15). Nothing said about secondary stress inside a single root.
new_statements.exceptions: None lexical. Morphological: suffixed verbs keep root-final stress (['ja.so], [pa.'ta.ko]), so word-final stress fails exactly when a suffix is present; trisyllabic monomorphemic roots exist (/ajagi/, /bagari/, /amara/) but no deviant stress is reported for them. Author caveat p.99 fn.3: sketch based mainly on a single speaker.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain explicitly the root morpheme, not the phonological word; transcriptions are citation forms from elicited lexicon (~900 items) and short texts. Equivalent alternative coding: 'morphologically determined' (root-final). Surveys by Schapper 2020 and Holton & Klamer 2018 summarise it as 'regular final stress'.
new_statements.identity_note: Klamer 2014 describes Kaera (kaer1234; the chapter notes it then had no ISO code, now jka) mainly from one speaker, Marianus Waang (b. Matgomi 1970, raised in Abang Iwang), i.e. the Abang Iwang variety of NE Pantar; alternative logonym Dorit. The author-site scan carries publisher pagination 97-146 (Glottolog's 76-114 for this chapter does not match the printed pages).
